text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Latvian MPs keep on changing factions. Six more deputies joined the faction of the Democratic Party Saimnieks, one joined the faction of the Farmers Union and another one - that of Fatherland & Freedom. As a result, the number of deputies in Democratic Party Saimnieks increased to 23 but the faction for People and Justice and the Latvian Unity Party ceased to exist.

- President Ulmanis continues his visit in Turkey. He visited the Mercedes Benz works in Turkey, and attended the meeting of the foreign affairs committee. It is expected that a free trade agreement may be signed in the near future.
- Latvia is visited by Princess Kristine Magnusen, the head of the Swedish Salvation Army.

- The newspaper notes that in 1986 the Latvian Supreme court, chaired at the time by MP Juris Kaksitis, sentenced to five years in prison a Latvian dissident, Rolands Silaraups. Now Kaksitis is one of the leaders of the Democratic Party Saimnieks and deputy prime minister.
- Five deputies submitted amendments to the citizenship law, which provides for abolishing existing age quotas and granting citizenship to those born in the future Latvia.
- Riga is hosting the second Baltic Book fair, which has opened at the Radisson SAS hotel.
- Latvia is visited by Finnish Trade and Industry Minister, Antti Kalliomaki, accompanied by a delegation representing Finnish big industries and small businesses.
- Officials from the ministries of culture of Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia signed a programme for cultural co-operation in the year 1997.
- The World Bank plans to allocate $200,000 as technical support to the Latvian State Control.
- The finance ministry has developed a forecast for economic development until the year 2002.
